title: EasyACIM: An End-to-End Automated Analog CIM with Synthesizable Architecture and Agile Design Space Exploration
problem: Current Analog Computing-in-Memory (ACIM) designs suffer from unscalable topologies and require heavy manual design effort. This limits application scenarios and increases time-to-market for ACIM systems.
motivation: ACIM is an emerging architecture for efficient AI inference at the edge, and automating its design can accelerate adoption and enable broader application coverage.
method: EasyACIM automates the entire process of designing analog computing-in-memory chips (specialized processors that perform calculations while storing data) by using an architecture that can be automatically synthesized from a specification. You provide the size of the computation array and a custom library of circuit building blocks, and the system automatically generates the complete physical layout. It uses a multi-objective genetic algorithm (a search technique that explores many design variations and keeps the best ones that balance competing performance goals) to find high-quality designs across different performance requirements and applications.
key_novelty: EasyACIM's core innovation is automating the entire design pipeline—from specification to physical layout—by combining a synthesizable architecture with MOGA-based design space exploration, which eliminates manual engineering and enables fast exploration of different solutions.
contributions: End-to-end automated ACIM design framework eliminating manual design efforts
Synthesizable ACIM architecture enabling scalability and automation
MOGA-based design space explorer for obtaining high-quality solutions across multiple objectives
Demonstration of wide design space with competitive performance versus state-of-the-art ACIM designs
